# Leap Day: February 29
## When Is the Next Leap Day?
The next leap day is [**February 29, 2028**](https://www.timeanddate.com/calendar/?year=2028) ; the last one was on [February 29, 2024](https://www.timeanddate.com/calendar/?year=2024) .

## Why Add a Leap Day?
Leap days are needed to keep our calendar in alignment with the Earth's revolutions around the Sun.
It takes the Earth approximately 365.242189 days—or 365 days, 5 hours, 48 minutes, and 45 seconds—to circle once around the Sun. This is called a tropical year .

# Which years are leap years?
## What is a leap year?
To be a leap year, the year number must be divisible by four – except for end-of-century years, which must be divisible by 400. This means that the year 2000 was a leap year, although 1900 was not.
**2028, 2032 and 2036** are all leap years.

### When is the next leap year and day?
The next leap year will be in **2024** , which means the next **leap day will be 29 February 2024** .

...

### Leap seconds
A leap second was added on 31 December 2005, the first since 1998, to help keep clock-time aligned with time measured by the Sun. Another was added in 2008, 2012 and 30 June 2015.

### How many hours in a leap year?
One leap year has 366 days. As each day has 24 hours, there are 8784 hours in a leap year in total.

# Is 2027 a Leap Year? No, and the Rule That Decides It
* No. 2027 is not a leap year. It is a common year with 365 days and 28 days in February.
* The reason is one line of arithmetic: 2027 is not divisible by 4, so it gets no leap day.
* The most recent leap year was 2024. The next one is 2028.
Leap years then continue every four years: 2032, 2036, 2040.

...

## The leap year rule, in one line
* **Divisible by 4?** Then it is a leap year. (2024, 2028, 2032 all pass.)
* **Divisible by 100?** Then it is not a leap year after all, even though it divides by 4. (1900 was a common year.)
* **Divisible by 400?** Then it is a leap year again. (2000 passed; 2400 will.)

...

## Leap years around 2027
Because leap years land every four years, the nearest ones bracket 2027 neatly. If you need the next leap year from wherever you are reading, it is 2028.
* **2024:** leap year (366 days). The most recent one.
* **2025, 2026, 2027:** common years (365 days each).
* **2028:** leap year. The next 29 February.
* **2032, 2036, 2040:** leap years, continuing the four-year step.

# Leap years, and why 2026 isn’t one
## Why 2026 isn’t a leap year
The last leap year was 2024. So 2028 will be our next leap year, a 366-day-long year, with an extra day added to our calendar (February 29). We’ll call that extra day a _leap day_ .
It’ll help synchronize our human-created calendars with Earth’s orbit around the sun and with the passing of the [seasons](https://earthsky.org/earth/can-you-explain-why-earth-has-4-seasons/) . Why do we need the extra day? Blame Earth’s orbit. Our planet takes approximately 365.25 days to orbit the sun once.

...

You can see that, if even more time were to pass without the leap year as a calendar correction, eventually February would be a summer month in the Northern Hemisphere.

* A mnemonic for remembering the years corresponding to leap years is: "גוחאדז"ט". The Hebrew letters Gimmel, Vav, Chet, Aleph, Dalet, Zayin, and Tet are used to represent the Hebrew numerals, 3,

...

## Gregorian Calendar Leap Years
* During a Gregorian calendar leap year, an additional day is added to February.
* A Gregorian year is a leap year if it meets BOTH criteria:
+ It is divisible by 4.
+ It is not divisible by 100, unless it is also divisible by 400.
* **2026 is not divisible by 4, and is therefore not a leap year.**
* **After 2026, the next leap year is 2028. 2028 is divisible by 4 and not by 100, and is therefore a leap year.**
* During a leap year, there are 366 days. During a non-leap year, there are 365 days.
